about: Namesakes split by hand: the tree joins people by name, so these are kept apart section by section (see annotate/merge.py, apply_namesakes).

groups.name: Perseus
groups.about: mythical hero, son of Zeus and Danae, slayer of Medusa, founder of Mycenae

groups.name: Perseus, king of Macedon
groups.about: last king of Macedon, son of Philip V, defeated by Rome

groups.name: Lynceus
groups.about: son of Aegyptus, husband of Hypermnestra, king of Argos

groups.name: Lynceus, son of Aphareus
groups.about: Messenian hero, brother of Idas, killed by Pollux

groups.name: Leotychides
groups.about: Leotychides II, Eurypontid king of Sparta, victor at Mycale

groups.name: Leotychides, son of Agis
groups.about: son of Agis II, kept from the throne by Agesilaus

groups.name: Clymene
groups.about: Clymene of the Trojan captives and of the altar with Dictys

groups.name: Clymene, mother of Homer
groups.about: said by the people of Ios to have been Homer's mother

groups.name: Clymene, daughter of Minyas
groups.about: daughter of Minyas, wife of Cephalus after Procris

groups.name: Niobe
groups.about: Niobe, daughter of Phoroneus, mother of Argus (and Pelasgus) by Zeus, in the Argive account.

groups.name: Niobe, daughter of Tantalus
groups.about: Niobe, daughter of Tantalus and wife of Amphion, whose children were slain and who was turned to stone on Mount Sipylus.

groups.name: Eubulus
groups.about: Eubulus, son of Carmanor, the Cretan and father of Carme.

groups.name: Eubulus, son of Spintharus
groups.about: A man buried at the place described, identified as the son of Spintharus; a different person from the Cretan son of Carmanor.

groups.name: Ægeus
groups.about: King of Athens, son of Pandion and father of Theseus, who sheltered Medea, drowned himself, and expelled settlers.

groups.name: Ægeus, son of Œolycus
groups.about: Spartan hero, son of Œolycus, a different person from the Athenian king.

groups.name: Polydorus
groups.about: Theban son and successor of Cadmus, father of Labdacus.

groups.name: Polydorus, king of Sparta
groups.about: Spartan king, son of Alcamenes and father of Eurycrates; popular and just, murdered by Polemarchus.

groups.name: Polydorus, adorner of the sacred wood
groups.about: Man said to have adorned the sacred wood with brass; identity unclear from the text, left separate.

groups.name: Sostratus
groups.about: Youth of Dyme, beloved of Heracles, called Acrochersites; the mythological figure the Wikipedia match fits.

groups.name: Sostratus, Sicyonian pancratiast
groups.about: Athlete of Sicyon known for breaking his opponents' fingers, nicknamed Acrochersites in some tradition.

groups.name: Sostratus, Chian sculptor
groups.about: Sculptor, father of Pantias.

groups.name: Antipater
groups.about: Macedonian general and regent, father of Cassander and Eurydice, who fought the Greeks in the Lamian War.

groups.name: Antipater, Milesian boxer
groups.about: Milesian boy who won the boxing victory at Olympia, son of Clinopater.

groups.name: Antipater, son of Cassander
groups.about: Son of Cassander who killed his mother Thessalonice.

groups.name: Lycus
groups.about: Theban regent, brother of Nycteus, guardian of Laius and husband of Dirce.

groups.name: Lycus, son of Pandion
groups.about: Athenian exile who fled from Aegeus, associated with the rites and oracles.

groups.name: Lycus, race-horse of the sons of Phidolas
groups.about: A horse owned by the sons of Phidolas.

groups.name: Lycus, Thracian boxer
groups.about: Thracian killed in a prize fight.

groups.name: Lycus, owner of a ruined house
groups.about: Former owner of a house that lay in ruins.

groups.name: Lycus, Messenian
groups.about: Messenian buried on the road.

groups.name: Ajax
groups.about: Ajax the Great, son of Telamon, hero of Salamis, whose death Teucer was held responsible for.

groups.name: Ajax, son of Oileus
groups.about: Ajax the Lesser, the Locrian hero who violated Cassandra at Athene's statue during the sack of Troy.

groups.name: Eteocles
groups.about: Theban son of Oedipus, brother of Polynices, killed him in single combat; father of Laodamas.

groups.name: Eteocles, king of Orchomenus
groups.about: Orchomenian king, son of Andreus (or Cephisus), father of Glaucon; first sacrificed to the Graces and died without male heirs.

groups.name: Eurytus
groups.about: Eurytus of Oechalia, son of Melaneus, father of Iole; honoured in Oechalia and his remains kept in a bronze urn.

groups.name: Eurytus, son of Actor
groups.about: Molionid Eurytus of Elis, son of Actor (with Theraphone and Thalpius), killed by Hercules.

groups.name: Electra
groups.about: Daughter of Agamemnon, sister of Orestes, wife of Pylades, mother of Medon and Strophius.

groups.name: Electra, daughter of Atlas
groups.about: The Pleiad, possibly the namesake of a river.

groups.name: Electra, sister of Cadmus
groups.about: Sister of Cadmus, who gave her name to a gate at Thebes.

groups.name: Electra, Helen's handmaid
groups.about: Servant of Helen, shown fastening her sandals.

groups.name: Thyia, daughter of Castalius
groups.about: Autochthon Castalius' daughter, first priestess of Dionysus, linked with Apollo as father of Delphus.

groups.name: Thyia of Orchomenus
groups.about: A woman of Orchomenus, distinct from the Delphic priestess.

groups.name: Pausanias
groups.about: Spartan regent, son of Cleombrotus, victor at Plataea, later disgraced.

groups.name: Pausanias, king of Sparta
groups.about: Spartan king, son of Pleistoanax and father of Agesipolis, who withdrew from Athens and went into exile at Tegea.

groups.name: Pausanias, the author
groups.about: The narrator and traveller who describes Greece in the first person.

groups.name: Pausanias, the Macedonian
groups.about: Macedonian accused of murdering Harpalus.

groups.name: Æneas
groups.about: Trojan hero, son of Anchises and Aphrodite, who escaped Ilium's fall, fought Diomede, and in Pausanias' traditions founded towns and carried the Palladium to Italy.

groups.name: Æneas, father of Thrasybulus
groups.about: Elean Æneas, father of the seer Thrasybulus.

groups.name: Thersander
groups.about: Theban king, son of Polynices and one of the Epigoni; took Thebes, was killed by Telephus, and was the father of Tisamenus.

groups.name: Thersander, son of Sisyphus
groups.about: Thersander son of Sisyphus, father of Haliartus and Coronus.

groups.name: Thersander, son of Agamedidas of Cleonae
groups.about: Thersander, king of the Cleonaeans, father of Lathria and Anaxandra.

groups.name: Aristodemus
groups.about: Heraclid son of Aristomachus, father of the twins Eurysthenes and Procles, who died before the Dorian return to the Peloponnese.

groups.name: Aristodemus, king of the Messenians
groups.about: Aepytid king of Messenia who sacrificed his daughter, led the defence at Ithome and killed himself.

groups.name: Aristodemus of Phigalia, tyrant of Megalopolis
groups.about: Phigalian son of Artylas, adopted by Tritaeus, who seized power in Megalopolis, defeated the Lacedaemonians and was called the Good.

groups.name: Aristodemus, son of Thrasis of Elis
groups.about: Elean wrestler, son of Thrasis.

groups.name: Aristodemus the Macedonian
groups.about: Macedonian commander leading Antigonus' mercenaries.

groups.name: Asterion
groups.about: Argive river-god, son of Oceanus and Tethys, who judged for Hera and was father of her nurses.

groups.name: Asterion, son of Cometes
groups.about: Argonaut, son of Cometes.

groups.name: Asterion, son of Minos
groups.about: Cretan Asterion, the Minotaur, son of Minos, killed by Theseus.

groups.name: Epeus
groups.about: Epeius, son of Panopeus, the Greek who built the Wooden Horse used to take Troy and is also credited with a wooden image of Hermes.

groups.name: Epeus, son of Endymion
groups.about: Elean king, son of Endymion, who won the kingdom by victory in a contest and gave the Epeans their name.

groups.name: Cypselus
groups.about: Tyrant of Corinth, son of Eetion and father of Periander; he drove out the Bacchidae and was hidden in the chest, and he dedicated a golden statue.

groups.name: Cypselus, king of the Arcadians
groups.about: Arcadian king, father of Merope, whom he married to Cresphontes; he founded Basilis.

groups.name: Cleombrotus
groups.about: Regent of Sparta c. 480-479 BC, son of Anaxandrides and brother of Leonidas; father of Pausanias, the victor at Plataea.

groups.name: Cleombrotus, king killed at Leuctra
groups.about: Later Spartan king who fell at the battle of Leuctra in 371 BC.

groups.name: Cleombrotus, son of Pausanias
groups.about: Young son of Pausanias, the Spartan regent and victor at Plataea.

groups.name: Aphrodite
groups.about: The goddess of love, worshipped under many cult titles at temples and statues throughout Greece.

groups.name: Celestial Aphrodite, daughter of Uranus
groups.about: Aphrodite Urania, the heavenly Aphrodite, whom Pausanias treats as the eldest and distinct from the daughter of Zeus, worshipped in Athens.

groups.name: Polydamas
groups.about: Trojan hero, son of Panthoos and companion of Hector, who killed Otus in the Trojan War.

groups.name: Polydamas, son of Nicias, athlete of Scotussa
groups.about: Giant pancratium victor from Scotussa (Scotusa), famed for his size and strength.

groups.name: Polydamas, father of Leocritus
groups.about: A man known only as the father of Leocritus; the book gives no other details, so he is kept separate from the Trojan and the athlete.

groups.name: Laodice
groups.about: Daughter of Priam and wife of Helicaon.

groups.name: Laodice, daughter of Agapenor
groups.about: Arcadian woman of Tegea, daughter of Agapenor, who sent a robe to Tegea and built the temple of Aphrodite.

groups.name: Alcamenes
groups.about: Sculptor of cult statues and temple sculpture (Hera, Aphrodite, Hecate, Asclepius, rear gables).

groups.name: Alcamenes, king of Sparta
groups.about: Spartan king, son of Teleclus and father of Polydorus.

groups.name: Alcamenes, Achaean officer
groups.about: Achaean officer sent to garrison Megara.

groups.name: Agesilaus
groups.about: Agesilaus II, Spartan king, son of Archidamus II and father of Archidamus III; lame half-brother of Agis, led the Asian expedition and died returning from Egypt.

groups.name: Agesilaus, early king of Sparta, son of Doryssus
groups.about: Early Spartan king, son of Doryssus and father of Archelaus, in whose reign Lycurgus legislated.

groups.name: Agesilaus of Lusi
groups.about: Native of Lusi in Arcadia, victor in a horse race.

groups.name: Aristocrates
groups.about: Arcadian king of Orchomenus, son of Hicetas, bribed by the Lacedaemonians in the Messenian war and a twice-proved traitor.

groups.name: Aristocrates, son of Aechmis
groups.about: Elder impious Arcadian king of Orchomenus, who violated a priestess of Artemis and was stoned by the Arcadians; his tomb is by the road.

groups.name: Ancæus
groups.about: King of the Leleges on Samos, son of Poseidon in the myth the Wikipedia match follows.

groups.name: Ancæus, son of Lycurgus
groups.about: Arcadian Argonaut, son of Lycurgus, who was wounded and killed by the Calydonian boar.

groups.name: Apollo
groups.about: The god of music, prophecy and the sun, worshipped under many cult epithets such as Carnean, Pythian, Maleatian, Spodius and Boedromius, with temples, statues and oracles throughout Greece, including Delphi.

groups.name: Thermius, brother of Oxylus
groups.about: A man called Thermius, brother of Oxylus, who was accidentally killed; not the god.

groups.name: Ismenius, son of Apollo
groups.about: A son of Apollo who gave his name to the river Ismenus at Thebes.

groups.name: Æschylus
groups.about: The Athenian tragic poet, son of Euphorion, who fought the Persians and whose plays Pausanias cites.

groups.name: Æschylus, father of Symmachus
groups.about: An Elean, named only as the father of Symmachus.

groups.name: Prometheus
groups.about: The Titan, son of Iapetus, giver of fire and maker of humans from clay, chained on the Caucasus and freed by Hercules; honored with an altar and torch race.

groups.name: Prometheus, one of the Cabiri
groups.about: A Cabiri figure at Thebes, father of Ætnæus, distinct from the Titan.

groups.name: Eurydice
groups.about: Daughter of Antipater and wife of Ptolemy I, mother of Lysandra; the Egyptian queen consort.

groups.name: Eurydice, wife of Philip
groups.about: Wife of Philip of Macedon, subject of a statue by Leochares in the Philippeum.

groups.name: Eurydice, wife of Orpheus
groups.about: Wife of Orpheus the Thracian singer.

groups.name: Eurydice, daughter of Lacedaemon
groups.about: Daughter of Lacedaemon and wife of Acrisius.

groups.name: Demeter
groups.about: The goddess of grain and harvest, mother of Proserpine, worshipped at many temples and in the Mysteries.

groups.name: Chthonia, sister of Clymenus
groups.about: Mortal at Hermione, sister of Clymenus (or daughter of Colontas), said to have built the temple of Demeter there.

groups.name: Thrasybulus
groups.about: Athenian general, son of Lycus, who put down the Thirty Tyrants.

groups.name: Thrasybulus, Elean seer
groups.about: Elean seer of the Iamidae, son of Aeneas, who prophesied victory; also the Elean linked to Pyrrhus's statue and Agathinus's father.

groups.name: Cleopatra
groups.about: Mythic daughter of Idas and Marpessa, wife of Meleager.

groups.name: Cleopatra, niece of Attalus
groups.about: Macedonian wife of Philip II, niece of Attalus, mother of Philip's baby boy.

groups.name: Cleopatra, daughter of Philip
groups.about: Macedonian princess, daughter of Philip, who built Telephanes's tomb.

groups.name: Cleopatra, Ptolemaic queen
groups.about: Queen who favoured her younger son, mother of Ptolemy Philometor and Alexander.

groups.name: Leonidas
groups.about: Leonidas I, Spartan king, son of Anaxandridas, who fell defending Thermopylae against the Persians.

groups.name: Leonidas II, king of Sparta
groups.about: Spartan king, son of Cleonymus, father of Cleomenes III and Epiclidas; deposed and restored in old age.

groups.name: Leonidas of Rhodes
groups.about: Rhodian runner who won twelve victories at the Olympic games.

groups.name: Leonidas of Elis
groups.about: Native of Elis who built the Hall (Leonidaeum) at Olympia.

groups.name: Gelon
groups.about: Gelon son of Dinomenes, tyrant of Gela and Syracuse, who defeated the Phoenicians (Carthaginians) and dedicated a chariot at Olympia.

groups.name: Gelon, son of Hiero II
groups.about: Son of Hiero II of Syracuse, who married Nereis.

groups.name: Gelon, Phocian leader
groups.about: Leader of the 300 picked Phocians killed by the Thessalians, a different man from the Sicilian rulers.
